name: Snake, Dread
body:
Dread Snake CR 7

XP 3,200
N Huge animal
Init +5; Senses low-light vision, scent; Perception +9

DEFENSE

AC 14, touch 8, flat-footed 14 (+6 natural, -2 size)
hp 87 (14d8+24)
Fort +8, Ref +3, Will +1

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft., swim 20 ft.
Melee bite +14 (3d6+4 plus poison)

STATISTICS

Str 19; Dex 11; Con 20; Int 1; Wis 13; Cha 2
Base Atk +10; CMB +10; CMD 16 (can’t be tripped)
Feats Improved Initiative, Weapon Finesse, Improved Natural Attack, Improved Natural Armor
Skills Acrobatics +9, Climb +9, Perception +9, Stealth +9, Swim +9; Racial Modifiers +4 Perception, +4 Stealth, +8 Acrobatics; modifies Climb and Swim with Dexterity

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Poison (Ex)

Bite—injury; save Fort DC 18; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect 1d4 Con; cure 1 save.

Spell-Like Abilities (Sp)

telepathic bond – at will, limited to only one bonded humanoid for dread snake’s lifetime.

ECOLOGY

Environment any temperate or warm
Organization solitary, pair, or nest (3–6)
Treasure none

The dread snake is a massive serpent that dwells near humanoids, especially bugbears, ogres, and the larger, more aggressive goblinoids. A dread snake will often choose the most capable warrior out of any given humanoid tribe and instinctually form a telepathic bond with this single humanoid. This telepathic bond is permanent, but the dread snake can only form a telepathic bond with a single intelligent creature during the dread snake’s lifetime. This imprinting is done by the dread snake, not the humanoid. The dread snake will become highly protective of its bonded partner, and will allow its partner to ride it as a mount.

If a dread snake’s bonded humanoid dies for any reason, the dread snake almost always goes berserk, and will enter into combat with any nearby creature. If the dread snake does not die in the conflict, after a period of 72 hours the snake will stop aggression and return to being a normal dread snake, albeit one that cannot telepathically bond again.

If the humanoid rejects the telepathic bond, the snake will attack the humanoid out of instinct, and then go berserk as above. In this rare circumstance, the dread snake also cannot telepathically bond again with any sentient being.

The average dread snake is over 50 feet long and weighs over 2,000 pounds. It has a scaled, patterned hide similar to a pit viper or asp.
